products.name: TESK
products.blurb: An implementation of the GA4GH Task Execution Service (TES) API that runs containerized tasks on any Kubernetes cluster.
products.description: TESK is a task execution engine based on the GA4GH TES standard that runs on Kubernetes. It exposes the TES endpoints, validates incoming task requests and translates them into Kubernetes batch jobs, so tasks run on any standard Kubernetes cluster. It can also stage task inputs and outputs and integrate with workflow managers.
features: Implements the GA4GH Task Execution Service (TES) API
Translates TES tasks into Kubernetes batch jobs
Designed to support any Kubernetes cluster
Handles task inputs and outputs using temporary persistent volume claims (PVCs) as scratch space
Integrates with workflow managers via an FTP account or an accessible PVC
Each task gets its own taskmaster, PVC and executor pods; only the API pod is shared across tasks
howItWorks: The API pod (Tomcat web server) receives and validates TES requests and turns them into Kubernetes jobs.
The API pod creates a taskmaster pod for each task.
The taskmaster starts a filer pod that creates a PVC as scratch space and downloads input files into the locations given in the TES request.
The taskmaster runs the executors as pods, one after the other.
The filer runs once more to push outputs to remote locations; then the PVC is scrubbed and deleted and the task completes.
requirements: A working Kubernetes cluster, version 1.9 or later
A default storage class supporting RWO mode (needed for tasks with I/O)
An FTP account or an accessible PVC (only for workflow-manager integration)

products.name: proTES
products.blurb: A GA4GH TES gateway that injects configurable middleware into task requests before forwarding them to independent TES nodes.
products.description: proTES is a scalable GA4GH TES API gateway that provides centralized features to a federated network of independently operated TES instances. When a TES request arrives, proTES applies the configured middlewares and then forwards it to a suitable TES instance. It can act as a compatibility layer, a load balancer, a public entry point to an enclave of compute nodes, or a way to collect telemetry. A plugin system makes it easy to write middlewares for access control, request/response processing or validation, and for choosing endpoints based on data-use restrictions and client preferences.
features: Flexible middleware injection through a plugin system
Federates containerized workloads across on-premise, hybrid and multi-cloud TES nodes
Built-in load balancing plugin (pro_tes.middleware.task_distribution.random) that distributes tasks randomly across TES endpoints
Built-in 'bring compute to the data' plugin (pro_tes.middleware.task_distribution.distance) that minimizes how far input data travels
OAuth2 bearer-token authorization out of the box
Declarative YAML configuration, based on the FOCA microservice archetype
Asynchronous tracking of forwarded tasks via RabbitMQ and scalable Celery workers
Helm chart for production and Docker Compose for development
quickStart: Open the Swagger UI at http://localhost:8080/ga4gh/tes/v1/ui
products.status: Beta; the API may change without notice

products.name: Cloud Registry
products.tagline: GA4GH Service Registry for the ELIXIR Cloud
products.blurb: An implementation of the GA4GH Service Registry API for registering and discovering GA4GH-compliant services in a federated cloud network.
products.description: Cloud Registry implements the GA4GH Service Registry API for the ELIXIR Cloud. Service entries comply with the ExternalService schema defined by the GA4GH Service Registry specification. Once deployed, the API is served under /ga4gh/registry/v1/ with an interactive Swagger UI at /ga4gh/registry/v1/ui, and it can be probed with simple HTTP calls, for example GET /services.
audience: Developers building on GA4GH service discovery
features: Implements the GA4GH Service Registry API
Service entries follow the GA4GH ExternalService schema
Interactive Swagger UI for exploring the API
Docker Compose deployment for development and testing
Helm chart for cloud-native deployments
Developer API documentation hosted on ReadTheDocs
products.status: Beta; the API may change without notice

products.name: Cloud Components
products.tagline: The component library for federated cloud services
products.blurb: Modular, customizable and extensible web components for building interfaces that interact with cloud infrastructure.
products.description: ELIXIR Cloud Components (ECC) is a library of web components for interacting with cloud infrastructure. Because they are standard web components, they are framework-agnostic and can be dropped into React, Vue, vanilla HTML or any other front-end stack. Components can be restyled to match your brand and extended with your own.
audience: Front-end developers building cloud service UIs
features: Built as web components, so they work in React, Vue, vanilla HTML and other frameworks
Modular and extensible, with documented guidance for making your own components
Themeable: brand color, corner radius, depth, density, sizing, font size and motion are configurable
Client components for GA4GH services, for example a WES runs component (@elixir-cloud/wes)
